Class Checkbox

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.AbstractPanelElement<Checkbox>
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.Checkbox
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public class Checkbox extends AbstractPanelElement<Checkbox>
A two-state boolean control rendered as a small square with a check-mark indicator and an adjacent label. The settings-ready convention for boolean interactions — pre-composed with a label, conventional visual.

Auto-sizes from label content: total width is BOX_SIZE + LABEL_GAP + fontWidth(label); total height is BOX_SIZE. Consumers do not pass width or height at construction; the element derives them from the label.

Clicking anywhere within the element bounds (square OR label area) toggles the state — matches HTML/native checkbox convention.

Rendering uses vanilla's icon/checkmark sprite for the checked indicator and MenuKit's PanelStyle.INSET for the box background. Resource packs that re-texture vanilla GUI sprites adapt MenuKit checkboxes automatically.

Mutable-state exception

Checkbox owns a mutable boolean, a narrow exception to MenuKit's declared-structure discipline. See Toggle for the full architectural justification; the same rationale applies here.

Dynamic-width limitation with supplier labels

The supplier-based constructor accepts a Supplier<Component> for dynamic label content. Auto-sizing elements with supplier-based variable content cannot guarantee layout stability — if the supplier returns different-length text each frame, the element's width changes per frame but panel layout is not re-resolved per frame. Consumers needing stable layout should use fixed-content variants or ensure the supplier returns same-width content across all evaluations (e.g., "Mode: AUTO" vs "Mode: MANUAL" where both strings render to similar widths).

Scope

  • Boolean only — no tri-state/indeterminate.
  • Fixed 10×10 checkbox square, sized to the 9×8 vanilla check-mark sprite. Larger checkboxes require custom PanelElement implementation.
  • No animation on state change.
  • Label text rendered in DEFAULT_LABEL_COLOR without shadow.

    • naturalWidth

      public int naturalWidth()
      Natural width = box + gap + the label's single-line rendered width — what the checkbox wants when the panel has room. The owning Panel maxes this across elements to find its hug-width; a wider element (or the screen-edge ceiling) then drives whether this label actually wraps. Identical to getWidth() in non-wrap mode, but kept distinct so a narrow pass can shrink presentation while natural intent stays put.

    • layoutWithin

      public void layoutWithin(int budget)
      Wrap the LABEL to the panel-assigned budget. The budget covers the whole element, so the label's own area is budget - BOX_SIZE - LABEL_GAP; we engage wrap ONLY when the label's natural single-line width exceeds that area, else clear it back to 0. Reversible: a later wider budget restores the single-line, box-centered label (same engage-only-when- natural-exceeds-available rule TextLabel uses).
      Parameters:
      budget - horizontal pixels available to this element, in panel content space. Always >= 1.

    • extraLayoutHeight

      public int extraLayoutHeight()
      Extra vertical pixels this checkbox occupies BEYOND its authored square because the label wrapped — i.e. getHeight() - BOX_SIZE, or 0 when not wrapped. The owning Panel reflows the elements below a wrapped checkbox downward by exactly this amount, so a label that grows from one line to two pushes — never paints over — what's beneath it.

    • mouseClicked

      public boolean mouseClicked(double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Called when the mouse is clicked on this element. The dispatcher hit-tests against the element's bounds before calling this method, so implementations know the click is within bounds.

      Returns true if this element consumed the click (preventing further dispatch to slots or vanilla). The default returns false, so render-only elements (TextLabel, Icon, ItemDisplay) don't need to override it.

      The button parameter is the mouse button: 0=left, 1=right, 2=middle. Core Button only consumes left-click; custom elements can handle any button.

      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y
      button - mouse button (0=left, 1=right, 2=middle)
      Returns:
      true if consumed, false to let the click fall through
